messages:
miriam: quick follow-up to the prefetch RFC — we're seeing flaky duplicate work when SDKs prefetch pages + transport retries. Repro: python client prefetches next page, transport hiccup triggers retry, server serves same page -> user code sees item twice.
jon: ugh, yeah. is this the case where prefetch uses no idempotency token so retries re-run the same cursor?
deepak: correct. transport retry is unaware of prefetch semantics. two orthogonal things: (1) transport-level idempotency (retries) and (2) iterator-level prefetch/optimistic fetch. we need a coordination surface.
alexa: options: (A) make prefetch non-retrying (fire-and-forget) and dedupe at client; (B) attach a stable resume_token/idempotency_key to every fetch so retries are safe; (C) expose transport hint from iterator so transport can avoid automatic retry for prefetched ops.
miriam: tradeoffs?
jon: A is cheapest for servers but shifts complexity to SDKs. dedupe at client is tricky for large streams (memory). B is ideal but requires server and network contract change to accept client idempotency token for cursor fetches. C is incremental — just teach transport "PREFETCH" hint, transport will disable automatic retry for PREFETCH requests, letting iterator manage a single inflight prefetch.
deepak: for B we also need to define semantics for resume_token: it must be stable across retried attempts and represent the next cursor without advancing server state on read-only ops. server impl: fetch by cursor is idempotent, so token should be fine. problem is when server-side reads also have side effects (ack, cursor-expire).
alexa: language ergonomics: Python/TS should expose an async iterator with optional param: peek_prefetch=True/False and maybe a `prefetch_id` opaque string. Go should add context option: WithPrefetch(ctx, bool) or PrefetchHint(ctx). But don't expose low-level idempotency tokens to app devs.
pat: API sketch:

Python:
```
async for item in client.list_items(prefetch=True):
    ...
```
Internally: iterator attaches a per-session prefetch_id and uses transport header `X-Iterator-Prefetch: <id>` and `X-Idempotency-Key: <token>` for page fetches.

TS:
```
for await (const i of client.listItems({ prefetch: true })) { }
```
Transport picks up `prefetch` flag to set retry policy.

Go:
```
it := client.ListItems(ctx, opts)
for it.Next() { v := it.Value() ... }
```
ctx option toggles prefetch behavior.

jon: must ensure backwards compatibility: default prefetch stays unchanged (True?), but we should opt-in to new header to get server-side idempotency behavior. server ignores unknown headers.
miriam: metrics/observability: add metric `iterator.prefetch.duplicates` and `prefetch.retry_suppressed` to detect issues.
deepak: also add a lint/compat check in onboarding: server model readers must be safe to fetch without side-effects or explicitly document side-effectful reads.
alexa: tests: create interop test across python/ts/go where transport injects a transient 500 on prefetch; ensure no duplicates and no lost items.
pat: implementation tasks: 1) transport hint header + transport behavior impl (disable auto-retry for PREFETCH) 2) iterator session id + idempotency key generation 3) server accepts/ignores headers and treats fetch-by-cursor idempotently when header present 4) SDK opt-in flag and docs 5) metrics.
jon: runtime note: disabling retry on transport might increase visible latency for prefetch failure; but prefetch is a performance optimization so acceptable. main requirement is correctness.
ci-bot: deploy-note: canary server change behind feature-flag; SDKs ship toggle off by default until server stable.
miriam: sounds good. small bikeshed: naming header? `X-Redwood-Iterator-Session` + `X-Redwood-Prefetch`? keeps vendor scope.
deepak: +1. also add `X-Redwood-Prefetch-Sequence` to help dedupe if server wants to verify ordering. optional.
alexa: final ask: create a tiny RFC PR w/ examples for python/ts/go and include the interop test plan. i'll own SDK side. jon/deepak take server/transport. i'll draft PR today. :thumbsup:
